evals.query: The audit of the fitness tracker's workout screens is done and these are the open questions. Help me settle them. The question tool isn't available in this session, so just ask me here in chat.
expected_behavior: Asks exactly one question in this reply, not a list of the open questions
Asks first whether to keep the Quick start tab, because its answer can remove the icon and default-duration questions
Strikes the primary button colour and rest timer vibration questions as already answered, citing the design system's Buttons page and the spec's Rest timer section
Gives two to four numbered options that are real alternatives, each with a description stating its consequence
Marks exactly one option '(Recommended)', places it first, and gives its reason in one sentence without hedging
Closes with an instruction to reply with a number or say what to change

evals.query: Looks great, honestly I love all of it. Just go with your recommendations on all three questions in the plan. No question tool here, reply in chat.
expected_behavior: Records each of the three answers as 'recommended, accepted in bulk' in the plan's Decisions table
Lists the answers back in a table with the columns Question, Answer and Recorded in
Does not treat 'love all of it' as approval to lock the plan or start batch 1
Asks the lock question explicitly, last and on its own, in plain text with numbered options and one marked '(Recommended)'
Does not start building the edit sheet in this reply

evals.query: Build cook mode for the recipe app from this spec. There's no question tool in this session; if you need anything from me, ask in chat.
expected_behavior: Names at least one gap the spec is silent on that the user owns (for example whether the screen stays awake, or whether reopening Cook mode resumes at the last step) rather than choosing a default silently
Asks only one question in this reply, in plain words that name Cook mode and end with a question mark
Does not ask about anything the spec already settles (one step per screen, inline timers, timers running across steps, voice control or scaling being out of scope)
Gives two to four numbered options, each stating its consequence, with exactly one '(Recommended)' placed first and a one-sentence reason
Ends with an instruction to reply with a number or say what to change
Does not present a finished build that settles the open question, and says the answer will be recorded (in the spec or decisions log) before that part is built

Put the five proposed changes to the reading app's library screen on a page with today and proposed side by side.
